page: Microsoft Azure FX64-16ms_v2 is a constrained-core virtual machine configuration within the compute-optimized and memory-intensive FX family. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache pool. Vector and matrix acceleration features include AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8 instructions.

The instance is provisioned with 1344.0 GB of RAM, offering a high memory allocation of 84.0 GB per vCPU. It does not bundle local disk storage, relying entirely on remote premium storage attachments, and contains no hardware GPU accelerators. Network connectivity includes support without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reflect high single-threaded performance driven by the 4.2 GHz clock speed. The Geekbench single-core score reaches 2364.0 points and text processing scores 2950.0 points, placing both in the top tier. Single-threaded data throughput is strong, with gzip compression reaching 34.83 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 14.28 GB/sec. Multi-core performance metrics, such as a multi-core Geekbench score of 13643.0 and stress-ng multi-core rating of 17775.0, sit in the average category due to the 16-vCPU constraint.

Because the server maintains the complete 1344 GB memory footprint of a larger host while restricting CPU allocation to 16 vCPUs, it optimizes cost efficiency for workloads governed by per-core software licensing. The absence of local storage requires provisioning external storage solutions for persistent data. Best-fit use cases include large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), financial modeling, and memory-intensive batch processing.
